evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.
A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusion summarises the design and launch uncertainty, but mostly restates earlier sections and inherits orbit and coverage errors. Some specific detail is present.
Clear headings and executive summary, but figures/tables are unnumbered, references are bare URLs and include Wikipedia, and writing/formatting flaws remain. Readable but not professional.

technical_issues.issue: Kourou latitude is given as 45.05°N; it is about 5.2°N. This contradicts the 'close to equator' claim and affects launch/orbit geometry.
Sun-synchronous inclination at 600 km should be about 97.8°, not 87.79°; the report's own plot implies ~97.7°. At 87.79° the orbit is prograde, not retrograde SSO.
RAAN initial value 27.33° is said to indicate launch location; RAAN is not simply launch-site longitude/latitude and needs launch-time/geometry justification.
Mean access duration shown is 580.786 s (9.7 min), not 'almost twenty minutes'; max is 12.8 min. Contact-frequency claims are overstated.
Drag-sail explanation is incomplete and no quantitative deorbit time or 25-year/space-debris compliance analysis is provided.
References are bare URLs and include Wikipedia, contrary to task instructions; citation formatting is incomplete.

overall: The report proposes a coherent coral-reef imaging mission with STK evidence, but core orbital-mechanics values and contact-duration claims are technically wrong. Referencing and required STK/PIGI files are incomplete; presentation is readable but unpolished.
